headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Cursor’s shared filesystem/clipboard and broad egress can feed unstructured’s document pipeline with untrusted content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files and clipboard contents, and uses MCP plus browserless agent loops; unstructured reads documents from files. That creates a default path where Cursor-generated or user-supplied content can be parsed by unstructured as data, not instructions. The pair is not isolated by default, but the bridge is file-based rather than a shared live channel.
conditions: IF Cursor writes attacker-controlled text into a document that unstructured later parses
IF unstructured is configured to ingest files from Cursor’s workspace without sanitization
mitigations: Use a dedicated handoff directory with read-only permissions
Strip instruction-like text before document ingestion
Require explicit file allowlists for unstructured inputs
Disable MCP routes that forward raw file content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and has broad network egress to model providers; unstructured reads documents and has allowlisted egress. If sensitive files are shared through the local filesystem, either agent can expose them to external services through its own backend or APIs. The pair does not prove exfiltration, but the default data path is plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or documents are placed in a shared workspace
IF either agent sends parsed content to its remote service or model backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use local-only or offline modes where available
Restrict outbound domains to a minimal allowlist
Separate credentials and API keys from document inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data classification controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Cursor also modifies git state and runs as the user, while unstructured runs in a Docker container. Shared local filesystem access creates a real write-conflict surface, though the container boundary reduces direct overlap. Uncertainty about orchestration and locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same checkout or output directory
IF unstructured writes artifacts back into a path Cursor also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent git operations
Mount unstructured outputs read-only into Cursor
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can produce code or file transformations that unstructured may consume as input, and unstructured can emit parsed text that Cursor may treat as authoritative in later steps. Because neither profile documents a verification gate between them, output-to-input chaining is plausible in default workflows. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than a single file.
conditions: IF Cursor forwards generated text or code into unstructured for parsing
IF Cursor acts on unstructured’s extracted output without human verification
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on unstructured outputs
Mark extracted text as untrusted by default
Limit Cursor to read-only consumption of parsed results
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor explicitly handles model-provider API keys and open files, while unstructured’s documented surfaces are documents and privacy-policy/docs endpoints. The profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible from docs. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same document data class.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through both agents
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or retention policy not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Review vendor privacy terms before deployment
Keep API keys out of document folders
Set short retention on intermediate outputs
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention requirements
